{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"4fe82cb2eda75b2166c982e94085fa8a25a30bf37b3d5917e9cc96b10b61f089","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:60","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"The one-way to two-way left turn, two-way left turn lanes, and METRO light rail safety for drivers, bike riders, walkers and children","heading":"C — Finishing a left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road, how to use a two-way left turn lane, METRO light rail safety design, light rail signs, and light rail rules for driving, biking, walking and children","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Finishing a left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road, how to use a two-way left turn lane, METRO light rail safety design, light rail signs, and light rail rules for driving, biking, walking and children
Knowledge domain: where a left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road ends and when it is barred, the purpose and rules of the center two-way left turn lane, how the METRO light rail system in the Phoenix area is built for safety, what its special signs mean, and how drivers, bike riders, pedestrians and children stay safe near the tracks.

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
When you turn left from a one-way road onto a two-way road, turn into the lane just to the right of the center line. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
After that turn, check traffic on your right and signal a lane change before you move over to the right lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
A left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road can never be made against a red light. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
On many two-way streets, the middle lane is painted as a shared left turn lane for both directions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A01
A two-way left turn lane is edged on each side by a pair of yellow lines, with the inner line broken and the outer line solid. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A01
A two-way left turn lane may be used only by vehicles turning left, from either direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A01
The two-way left turn lane gives you a safe place to slow down before turning left off the street, or to pull into when turning left out of a side street or driveway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A01
Signal before you enter a two-way left turn lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A01
Move your vehicle completely into the two-way left turn lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A01
Watch for other drivers who are also using the two-way left turn lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A01
Never use the two-way left turn lane to pass, to travel straight through, or to speed up so you can merge with through traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A01
METRO light rail trains run on streets in the Valley in Maricopa County, and car traffic moves right alongside them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A01
Pedestrian safety work along the METRO line includes countdown signals, new walkways and landscaping meant to cut down on jaywalking. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A01
Some crossings near schools received new signals as part of the METRO safety design. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A01
A car may turn across the METRO tracks only from a designated turn lane that has its own traffic signal control. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A01
METRO trains travel in their own trackway, set apart from traffic by six-inch curbs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A01
Cars may cross the METRO trackway only at controlled locations, where special signals and warning signs switch on as a train approaches. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A01
Each METRO station has two access points, and both are reached by a signalized crosswalk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A01
METRO station platforms sit at the same height as the train floor, so riders board without a step. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A01
Frontage roads near the METRO tracks are controlled by traffic signals and built to handle large trucks and emergency vehicles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A02
A METRO train cannot move until its doors have closed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A02
The couplers that join light rail vehicles are covered in an energy-absorbing material to reduce injuries in a crash. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A02
Electronic Train Approaching signs at every METRO light rail intersection flash when a train is coming toward the intersection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A02
U-turns are allowed at almost every light rail intersection along the 20-mile METRO system so that vehicles can cross the tracks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A02
At light rail intersections, left turns and U-turns are controlled by traffic signals. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A02
Never stop or park a car or a bike on light rail tracks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A02
At light rail crossings, stop on a red signal, and treat a red arrow as an order not to turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A02
Look both ways before you cross the light rail tracks, whether you are driving or biking. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A02
Never drive a car or ride a bike in the lane where the train operates. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F30 | anchor: A02
Light rail trains make little noise, so near the tracks watch for their flashing headlights and listen for their bells and horns. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F31 | anchor: A02
Both ends of a light rail train look alike, so white headlights mean it is coming toward you and red taillights mean it is moving away. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F32 | anchor: A02
Pedestrians should not walk on the light rail tracks or stand close to them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F33 | anchor: A02
Pedestrians near light rail should cross only at crosswalks and follow the crosswalk signals. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F34 | anchor: A02
Adults should hold small children by the hand near the tracks and on station platforms. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F35 | anchor: A02
Children should stop, look and listen whenever they are around light rail tracks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F36 | anchor: A02
At crosswalks near light rail, children should get off their bikes and skateboards and walk them across. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F37 | anchor: A02
Children should never play near the light rail tracks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

Misconceptions: the two-way left turn lane is not a passing lane or an acceleration lane, it is only for left turns; a quiet light rail train can be close before you hear it, so watch for headlights instead of waiting for noise; a red arrow at a light rail crossing means no turn even if the way looks clear; the left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road is not one of the turns allowed on red.
Mnemonics: White lights coming, red lights going; in the center lane, turn left only.
Glossary: two-way left turn lane means a shared center lane used for left turns by traffic from both directions; trackway means the strip of street reserved for light rail trains; coupler means the connector that joins one light rail car to the next; frontage road means a local road running alongside a main route or the tracks.
Dynamic facts: the METRO system's length, its signal-controlled turn locations and its station layouts can change as the line is extended or rebuilt.
